findings.problem: The hand-written Star Wars schema shown in 'The Schema' section contradicts the real demo schema that the very same page inlines a few lines below via the `#schema` snip (println(... snip("demo/src/main/scala/demo/starwars/StarWarsMapping.scala", "#schema"))). The page presents two different, conflicting versions of the same schema. Concretely the hand-written block declares `hero(episode: Episode!): Character`, `id: ID!`, `name: String!`, `friends: [Character]`, `appearsIn: [Episode]!`, whereas the actual demo source (and the inlined snip) declare `hero(...): Character!`, `id: String!`, `name: String`, `friends: [Character!]`, `appearsIn: [Episode!]`. Because the page also uses integer id literals like `character(id: 1000)` / `character(id: 1002)`, those are only valid under the shown `id: ID!`; against the real `id: String!` an Int literal would not coerce, so the divergence is load-bearing and misleads the reader about the schema they are actually running.
findings.fix: Make the hand-written SDL block match the demo source exactly: `hero(episode: Episode!): Character!`, and on Character/Human/Droid use `id: String!`, `name: String`, `friends: [Character!]`, `appearsIn: [Episode!]`. (Or drop the hand-written block entirely and rely on the `#schema` snip already inlined below it, so there is a single source of truth.) If you keep `id: ID!`, then also change the demo source — but the simplest fix is to align the prose schema to the snip.

findings.problem: `DoobiePgMapping` and `SkunkMapping` are `abstract class`es in the source (modules/doobie-pg/src/main/scala/DoobiePgMapping.scala:25 `abstract class DoobiePgMapping[F[_]](...)`; modules/skunk/shared/src/main/scala/SkunkMapping.scala:34 `abstract class SkunkMapping[F[_]](...)`), not traits. The mixin traits are `DoobiePgMappingLike[F]` / `SkunkMappingLike[F]`. As written, `trait MyDoobieMapping[F[_]] extends DoobiePgMapping[F]` would not compile (a trait cannot extend an abstract class with a constructor), and the later `new DoobiePgMapping[F](transactor, monitor) with MyDoobieMapping[F]` would attempt to inherit the same abstract class twice. The page already labels the block "illustrative rather than compiled," which limits the harm, but the word "trait" is factually wrong for these names.
findings.fix: Call `DoobiePgMapping`/`SkunkMapping` what they are: "abstract base classes." For the user-mapping sketch, mix in the `*Like` trait instead, mirroring the demo pattern, e.g. `trait MyDoobieMapping[F[_]] extends DoobiePgMappingLike[F] { ... }` and `new DoobiePgMapping[F](transactor, monitor) with MyDoobieMapping[F]`, and likewise `trait MySkunkMapping[F[_]] extends SkunkMappingLike[F]` with `new SkunkMapping[F](pool, monitor) with MySkunkMapping[F]`.
